# Post new and updated Jira issues to Discord

**Pattern:** Event -> route -> notify · **Level:** Production · **Trigger:** Jira webhook

## What it does
Turns Jira issue activity — created and updated — into readable Discord messages, each with fitting wording.

## Why it exists
A dev team shouldn't have to sit in Jira to know what changed. This pushes issue activity into Discord in seconds, with the right phrasing for a new issue vs an update.

## Main flow
Jira Issue Webhook -> Extract Issue Fields -> Created or Updated? -> Format message -> Post to Discord (failure -> error rail).

## Use it for
- A team that triages in Jira but chats in Discord
- Announcing issues reaching Done without a standup
- Read-only issue visibility for non-Jira stakeholders

## You get
- Jira activity in Discord within seconds
- Fitting wording per event
- Retried, surfaced failures

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Jira API token; Discord webhook URL.
Colour key: 🟦 entry · 🟫 app I/O · ⬜ logic · 🟩 output · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
This is event-driven; sample events (a created bug, an updated story) are pinned so you can run it with no credential. Sample data is pinned on the trigger, so hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow end to end before attaching a single credential. Right-click → Unpin when you go live.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never bundled in a template. Every node that talks to an external service needs its own connection before the first real run — open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Jira API token**
Atlassian → account settings → Security → API tokens → Create. n8n's Jira SW Cloud credential takes your account email, the token, and your site URL (https://your-domain.atlassian.net).
_Gotcha:_ The token inherits your Jira permissions — it can only read/write projects your own account can access.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy Webhook URL. Paste it into n8n's Discord Webhook credential.
_Gotcha:_ A webhook URL is bound to one channel. Use a separate webhook/credential per channel you post to.

Set each credential up once; it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens when the event should fire**
Cause: The workflow is still a draft, or its trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate it. The manual test URL is different from the production URL.

**A node shows a red triangle right after import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials note).

**No events arrive**
Cause: The Jira webhook didn't register, or points at the wrong events.
Fix: Jira needs a publicly reachable callback — activate the workflow. Confirm the webhook events include issue_created / issue_updated.

**The browse link is wrong**
Cause: JIRA_BASE_URL isn't set, so it falls back to the placeholder domain.
Fix: Set JIRA_BASE_URL to your https://your-domain.atlassian.net site URL.

**Discord posts nothing / returns 400**
Cause: The message content resolved to an empty string, or the webhook URL is wrong.
Fix: Discord rejects empty content. Check the upstream expression produced text, and re-copy the webhook URL.

Still stuck? The **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there.

## Design decisions

Created and updated are split by the webhookEvent string, not by inspecting field changes, because Jira tells you the event type directly and that keeps the branch simple. The browse URL is built from an env var so the same template works across sites without editing the graph. Discord runs in webhook mode so nothing has to be installed in the server.

## Practice exercises

Already production-shaped — deepen it:

1. Route issues by project key to different Discord channels.
2. Only post updates that change the status field, using the changelog in the payload.
3. @mention the assignee by mapping their Jira account to a Discord ID.

## 🛠 Customize me

Watched events (`issue_created`/`issue_updated`) are on **Jira Issue Webhook**; the browse link uses `JIRA_BASE_URL`. Created vs updated wording is in the two Format nodes. Route by project key to different channels, or post only status-change updates using the changelog in the payload.

## 🔐 Security

Use a Jira service account scoped to the relevant project(s); the token inherits its permissions. Issue summaries can contain sensitive detail, so post to a private channel. The Discord webhook URL stays in the credential, never a node parameter.
